verdict: Real CLI supports stable module-based configuration regeneration with retained state; state regeneration, universal adoption and cleanup by omission are not supported by these probes.
counterexamples: local_file rejects import; a subsequent create overwrites pre-existing execution-created content.
Lost state plans creates and changes a built-in binding identity; identical regenerated configuration can overwrite independently changed content.
Omitting an orphaned resource's provider alias blocks destruction until the alias is restored.
Removing a resource block skips its destroy provisioner; retained count=0 runs the benign cleanup hook.
Declarative import can include update actions, while CLI import exposes an ID output immediately but leaves imported configured values null until reconciliation.
Renaming an installation key plans delete/create despite otherwise equivalent module material.
positive_results: Two instances share stored HCL material with isolated state addresses and explicit provider mappings.
Repeated apply and reordered-key root regeneration preserve outputs with all no-op plan actions.
Removing one instance retains the other and the shared declaration; executed final destruction follows reversed dependencies.
evidence_boundary: terraform_data is a real CLI state-only surrogate, not an external-artifact adoption proof; fixture copying models DML materialization without implementing it.
documentation: Context7 quota exceeded; primary OpenTofu documentation and pinned local provider source docs used.
priority_gaps: State durability and provider-specific preservation gates
Stable declaration IDs and cleanup provider retention
Incomplete binding publication and import drift
Durable cleanup and shared retention aggregation
next_experiment: Use an import-capable sandbox-file provider to test mismatched adopted attributes and recovery across import, binding publication and cleanup.
